# Microservices Architecture: Internal Security Middleware Hub

## Background

**Platform name: Internal Security Middleware Hub**

Each app is a **separate container** with a **central Hub** for choosing which app to enter:

1. **Hub** â€” Landing portal with app-switcher and centralized authentication
2. **DefectDojo Viewer** â€” Existing vulnerability workflow (minimal changes)
3. **Wazuh Viewer** â€” New incident/SIEM workflow (**frontend-only mockup first** â€” no backend API yet)

Each service can be brought **up/down independently**.

---

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TB
    User["Browser"] --> Gateway["Nginx Gateway\n:80"]
    
    Gateway -->|"/"| Hub["Hub Service\n:3000\n(Express + React)"]
    Gateway -->|"/defectdojo/*"| DDojo["DefectDojo Service\n:3001\n(Express + React)"]
    Gateway -->|"/wazuh/*"| Wazuh["Wazuh Service\n:3002\n(Static React only)\nMockup Phase"]
    
    Hub --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
    DDojo --> DB

    style Gateway fill:#6366f1,color:#fff
    style Hub fill:#172033,stroke:#6366f1,color:#f1f4f9
    style DDojo fill:#172033,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#f1f4f9
    style Wazuh fill:#172033,stroke:#22c55e,color:#f1f4f9
    style DB fill:#0f1624,stroke:#2d3748,color:#f1f4f9
```

> [!TIP]
> **Wazuh has no backend and no DB connection in the mockup phase.** It's just a static React app with hardcoded mock data served by a lightweight static server. This lets you design the UI and navigation flow before committing to any API contract.

---

## Docker Compose â€” Per-Service Control

```bash
# â”€â”€â”€ Start/stop individual services â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose up -d hub              # Hub only
docker compose up -d defectdojo       # DefectDojo only
docker compose up -d wazuh            # Wazuh only (static frontend)
docker compose up -d gateway          # Gateway only
```

Each page works with the mock data â€” you can navigate, filter, click into details, but no data persists (state resets on refresh):

## Remaining Architecture (Unchanged)

### Hub Service
- Express backend: login, logout, user management, app registry
- React frontend: login page, app card grid with health status
- Brand: **Internal Security Middleware Hub**

### DefectDojo Changes (Minimal)
- Swap session auth â†’ JWT middleware
- Remove login/user routes (Hub handles this)
- Add `base: '/defectdojo/'` in Vite
- Add "Back to Hub" nav item

### Gateway (Nginx)
- `/` â†’ Hub, `/defectdojo/*` â†’ DefectDojo, `/wazuh/*` â†’ Wazuh
- Rate limiting, security headers
- Graceful 502 when a backend is down

### Security & Performance
- JWT auth (1hr TTL), shared `JWT_SECRET`
- Network isolation (only gateway exposes ports)
- Resource limits per container
- Non-root containers
- HTTP only (HTTPS when domain is ready)

## Execution Plan

| Phase | Scope | Effort |
|-------|-------|--------|
| **Phase 1** | Monorepo, shared auth (JWT), gateway, Hub service | ~2â€“3 days |
| **Phase 2** | Migrate DefectDojo â†’ `defectdojo/` dir, JWT swap, base path | ~1â€“2 days |
| **Phase 3** | Wazuh frontend mockup (all pages, mock data, routes, styling) | ~3â€“4 days |
| **Phase 4** | Docker Compose orchestration + full-stack testing | ~1 day |
| **Phase 5** | Security hardening | ~1â€“2 days |
| *Phase 6 (future)* | *Wazuh backend API + real Wazuh integration* | *~3â€“5 days* |

**Total for mockup-ready platform: ~8â€“12 days**

### Per-Service Independence

```bash

curl http://localhost/defectdojo/api/health          # Still works âœ…
curl http://localhost/wazuh/                         # 502 (expected) âœ…
docker compose up -d wazuh                          # Back online âœ…
```

### Manual

1. Hub â†’ login â†’ see app cards (DefectDojo âœ…, Wazuh âœ…)
2. Click DefectDojo â†’ works as before
3. Click Wazuh â†’ dashboard with mock data â†’ navigate alerts/incidents/agents
4. Stop Wazuh container â†’ Hub shows "Offline" â†’ DefectDojo unaffected
5. Start Wazuh â†’ Hub shows "Healthy" again

## Design Direction

The Hub follows the existing **Cobalt Bunker** design system from DefectDojo Viewer: deep space blue background, flat tonal layering, cobalt indigo accents, Prompt font family, and high-contrast text. No gradients on cards, no glassmorphism (except the login card which matches the existing pattern).

Each app workspace gets its own **accent color** for identity:
- DefectDojo: **Amber** (#f59e0b)
- Wazuh: **Green** (#22c55e)
- Hub/Platform: **Cobalt** (#6366f1)

FROM node:22-alpine AS deps

WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci

FROM deps AS build

WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:22-alpine AS runtime

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    PORT=3000 \
    DATA_DIR=/app/data

WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev && npm cache clean --force

COPY --from=build /app/backend ./backend
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist

RUN mkdir -p /app/data && chown -R node:node /app
USER node

EXPOSE 3000

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \
  CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health || exit 1

CMD ["node", "backend/server.cjs"]

services:
  gateway:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "${GATEWAY_PORT:-80}:80"
    volumes:
      - ./gateway/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
    depends_on:
      hub:
        condition: service_healthy
      defectdojo:
        condition: service_healthy
      wazuh:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped

  hub:
    build: ./hub
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      PORT: 3000
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://${PG_USER:-defectdojo}:${PG_PASSWORD:-change-me}@db:5432/${PG_DB:-defectdojo_viewer}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:-dev-secret-key-change-me-in-production}
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256M
          cpus: "0.5"
    restart: unless-stopped

  defectdojo:
    build: ./defectdojo
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      PORT: 3001
      DATA_DIR: /app/data
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://${PG_USER:-defectdojo}:${PG_PASSWORD:-change-me}@db:5432/${PG_DB:-defectdojo_viewer}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:-dev-secret-key-change-me-in-production}
    volumes:
      - defectdojo-data:/app/data
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512M
          cpus: "1.0"
    restart: unless-stopped

  # Wazuh â€” static frontend only (no backend, no DB)
  wazuh:
    build: ./wazuh
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3002/"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 128M
          cpus: "0.25"
    restart: unless-stopped

  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${PG_DB:-defectdojo_viewer}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${PG_USER:-defectdojo}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${PG_PASSWORD:-change-me}
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512M
          cpus: "1.0"
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  defectdojo-data:
  postgres-data:

ArtifactMetadata.Summary: Comprehensive user guide explaining the system architecture, the SSO authentication workflow, and Docker Compose commands for running the services independently.

Args.CodeContent:
# User Guide: Internal Security Middleware Hub

This guide explains how the newly migrated **Internal Security Middleware Hub** monorepo works under the hood, how the single sign-on (SSO) authentication behaves, and how to manage the services independently.

---

## 1. System Architecture

The platform has been restructured into a decoupled, microservices-ready monorepo:

```mermaid
graph TB
    Browser["User Browser"] -->|"Port :80"| Gateway["Nginx Gateway\n(gateway)"]
    
    Gateway -->|"/"| Hub["Hub Portal\n(hub)\n:3000"]
    Gateway -->|"/defectdojo/*"| DefectDojo["DefectDojo Viewer\n(defectdojo)\n:3001"]
    Gateway -->|"/wazuh/*"| Wazuh["Wazuh Mockup\n(wazuh)\n:3002"]
    
    Hub -->|"Shared Auth Tables"| DB[(PostgreSQL)]
    DefectDojo -->|"Sync Records"| DB
    
    style Gateway fill:#6366f1,color:#fff
    style Hub fill:#172033,stroke:#6366f1,color:#f1f4f9
    style DefectDojo fill:#172033,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#f1f4f9
    style Wazuh fill:#172033,stroke:#22c55e,color:#f1f4f9
    style DB fill:#0f1624,stroke:#2d3748,color:#f1f4f9
```

1. **Nginx Gateway (`gateway`)**: The single entry point exposing port `80`. It routes requests dynamically to backend containers using path prefixes and strips prefixes automatically.
2. **Central Hub (`hub`)**: Renders the login portal and the application switcher interface.
3. **DefectDojo Viewer (`defectdojo`)**: Vulnerability workflow tracker (migrated into a sub-directory).
4. **Wazuh Viewer (`wazuh`)**: Interactive incident and agent monitoring frontend mockup.
5. **PostgreSQL Database (`db`)**: Shared relational store.

---

## 2. Centralized Authentication (Single Sign-On - SSO)

The platform has transitioned from stateful session cookies to a **stateless JWT-based SSO** architecture:

```
[1. User Logs In] â”€â”€> Hub Backend verifies password â”€â”€> Signs JWT with JWT_SECRET
                                                               â”‚
[3. Browser Redirects] <â”€â”€ Saves token in localStorage <â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜
  â”‚
  â”œâ”€â”€> Enters DefectDojo â”€â”€> Reads token â”€â”€> API calls include: Authorization: Bearer <JWT>
  â”‚                                            â”‚
  â”‚                                            â””â”€â”€> DefectDojo Backend verifies JWT signature
  â”‚
  â””â”€â”€> Enters Wazuh Mockup â”€â”€> Reads token â”€â”€> Verifies auth presence locally
```

### The Authentication Flow:
1. **Login**: You navigate to `http://localhost/`. The Nginx gateway forwards you to the **Hub Service**.
2. **Token Issuance**: When you sign in, the Hub backend verifies your password (PBKDF2 SHA-512) against the Postgres database. It signs a stateless **JSON Web Token (JWT)** containing your username, role, and authorized products, valid for 1 hour.
3. **SSO Storage**: The Hub frontend stores this token in browser `localStorage` under `middleware_token` and `middleware_user`.
4. **Workspace Handover**: When you select a workspace (e.g., clicking *DefectDojo Viewer*), the browser redirects to `http://localhost/defectdojo/`.
5. **Session Reading**: The DefectDojo React app reads the same `middleware_token` from your browser storage. It prepends this token inside the `Authorization` header (`Bearer <token>`) for all database/API calls.
6. **Stateless Verification**: The DefectDojo backend verifies the signature of the incoming JWT locally using the shared `JWT_SECRET`. No API calls to the Hub container are needed!
7. **Session Expiry**: If you log out or your token expires, the client clears the local storage keys and redirects you back to the Hub landing page (`/`).

---

## 3. How to Use the Containers

Each service container is isolated and can be started, stopped, or rebuilt independently without breaking the rest of the application.

### Basic Commands

Run these commands in the root directory where the `docker-compose.yml` file is located:

```bash
# â”€â”€â”€ Start the entire stack â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose up -d

# â”€â”€â”€ Stop the entire stack â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose down

# â”€â”€â”€ Rebuild all containers â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose up -d --build
```

### Independent Service Control

If you are modifying code in only one service, you can bring it up or down without taking down other containers:

```bash
# â”€â”€â”€ Stop a single service â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose stop wazuh          # Wazuh goes down, DefectDojo/Hub remain active

# â”€â”€â”€ Start/Restart a single service â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose up -d wazuh         # Re-activates Wazuh container
docker compose restart defectdojo  # Restarts DefectDojo backend

# â”€â”€â”€ Rebuild a single service â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose up -d --build hub   # Rebuilds and updates Hub code only

# â”€â”€â”€ Check active container statuses â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose ps

# â”€â”€â”€ Stream live logs for a single container â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
docker compose logs -f defectdojo
```

---

## 4. Wazuh Frontend Mockup Walkthrough

The **Wazuh Viewer** (`http://localhost/wazuh/`) operates as a React prototype serving realistic security incident logs:

* **Dashboard**: Displays active incident counters, critical alerts, and live agent status metrics.
* **Alerts Log**: Filter alerts by threat level (Low, Medium, High, Critical) and search by rules or IPs. Clicking any alert row opens a detail panel displaying the JSON log payload.
* **Incident Management**:
  * View open security incidents (e.g., SSH brute force, web shell injections).
  * Click into an incident to view its **Activity Timeline** history.
  * You can **change the status** of an incident (e.g., Open âž” Investigating âž” Resolved) using the dropdown.
  * You can **add timeline notes** and post updates. The timeline will instantly display your username and timestamp. *(Note: Data is saved in memory and will reset on page refresh).*
  * Click **New Incident** to manually report a new security event.
* **Agents**: Monitored endpoints inventory showing IP addresses, operating systems, and agent statuses.

Args.CodeContent:
# Internal Security Middleware Hub

A high-performance, containerized microservices suite that serves as a centralized single sign-on (SSO) gateway and dashboard switcher for internal security tools, including **DefectDojo Viewer** and a mockup of the **Wazuh Viewer**.

---

## System Architecture

The suite consists of five containers orchestrated via Docker Compose:

```mermaid
graph TB
    User["Browser (http://localhost)"] --> Gateway["Nginx Gateway\n(Port :80)"]
    
    Gateway -->|"/"| Hub["Hub Service\n(Port :3000)\nExpress + React"]
    Gateway -->|"/defectdojo/*"| DDojo["DefectDojo Service\n(Port :3001)\nExpress + React"]
    Gateway -->|"/wazuh/*"| Wazuh["Wazuh Service\n(Port :3002)\nStatic React + Nginx"]
    
    Hub --> DB[(PostgreSQL 16)]
    DDojo --> DB

    style Gateway fill:#6366f1,color:#fff
    style Hub fill:#172033,stroke:#6366f1,color:#f1f4f9
    style DDojo fill:#172033,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#f1f4f9
    style Wazuh fill:#172033,stroke:#22c55e,color:#f1f4f9
    style DB fill:#0f1624,stroke:#2d3748,color:#f1f4f9
```

### 1. Nginx Gateway (`gateway` Â· Port `80`)
The main gateway of the system. It handles:
- **Routing**: Proxy-passes requests from the browser to the backend services based on subpaths (`/` for Hub, `/defectdojo/` for DefectDojo, `/wazuh/` for Wazuh).
- **DNS Resolution**: Dynamically re-resolves container hostnames at runtime using Docker's internal DNS resolver (`127.0.0.11`) to prevent broken gateways when containers restart or receive new IPs.
- **SSE Buffering**: Disables proxy buffering for Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream endpoints (`/defectdojo/api/sync/events`) to enable real-time synchronization.
- **Security Headers**: Injects headers (`X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-XSS-Protection`, `Referrer-Policy`) and enforces rate limiting (5r/s) on `/api/login` to prevent brute force attacks.

### 2. SSO Hub Service (`hub` Â· Port `3000`)
The entry point switcher portal:
- **Backend (Express)**: Manages database connection, initializes the shared `defectdojo_viewer_users` schema, and handles login. It issues stateless HMAC-SHA256 JWT tokens valid for 1 hour.
- **Frontend (React)**: Split-screen brand layout login page + landing portal switcher card grid. Dynamically checks client-side health by querying endpoints (`/defectdojo/api/health` and `/wazuh/`) and displaying status badges (Healthy/Offline).

### 3. DefectDojo Viewer (`defectdojo` Â· Port `3001`)
Vulnerability workflow management tool:
- **Backend (Express)**: Validates incoming requests by verifying the shared JWT token against a shared `JWT_SECRET`. Connects to the database to sync and store findings.
- **Frontend (React)**: Displays pulled vulnerability findings, CVE compactions, and coordinates ticket workflows with Redmine. A "Back to Hub" nav item is integrated to return to the portal switcher.

### 4. Wazuh Viewer (`wazuh` Â· Port `3002`)
A frontend-only static mockup representing the SIEM & incident management dashboard:
- **Frontend (React)**: Interactive dashboard, filterable alerts feed, incident creation form, OS agent grid, and investigation timelines built from realistic mockup datasets.
- **Runtime (Nginx)**: Serves static compiled React assets. Validates auth token presence in `localStorage` on the frontend before loading.

### 5. Shared Database (`db` Â· Port `5432` internally)
A PostgreSQL 16 database shared between the Hub and DefectDojo containers. User accounts are created on the Hub, written to the database, and read transparently by both services.

---

## Single Sign-On (SSO) Mechanism

Because all containers are served behind the Nginx Gateway on port 80 under the same domain host (`http://localhost`), they share a **single origin**. 

1. When the user logs in at `http://localhost/`, the Hub backend issues a JWT token.
2. The Hub frontend saves this token in `localStorage` under `middleware_token` and the user profile under `middleware_user`.
3. When the user clicks on **DefectDojo Viewer** (`/defectdojo/`) or **Wazuh Viewer** (`/wazuh/`), the browser retains the shared `localStorage` state.
4. Each service extracts `middleware_token` from `localStorage` and appends it to requests as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
5. The backend validates the signature using the shared `JWT_SECRET` key, completing the stateless SSO flow.

---

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites
- Docker and Docker Compose installed.

### Setup and Start

1. **Configure Environment Variables**:
   Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and configure your settings:
   ```powershell
   Copy-Item .env.example .env
   ```

2. **Boot the Orchestration Stack**:
   Start all containers in detached mode:
   ```powershell
   docker compose up -d --build
   ```

3. **Access the Application**:
   Open **`http://localhost`** in your browser.
   - **Default Credentials**: 
     - **Username**: `admin`
     - **Password**: `admin`

---

## How to Use & Operations

### Independent Service Control
You can start, stop, or rebuild individual containers without affecting others. The Nginx gateway dynamically handles backend failover:

```powershell
# Stop a single service to test offline states
docker compose stop defectdojo

# Hub switcher dashboard will dynamically update the card status badge to "Offline"
# Restart the service to bring it back online
docker compose start defectdojo

# Rebuild a single service after making changes (e.g. Wazuh frontend)
docker compose up -d --build wazuh
```

### User Management
User administration is centralized:
- Log in as the `admin` user.
- Click **User Management** in the administration section of the Hub.
- The Hub API interacts with the shared PostgreSQL table to execute user CRUD operations immediately, which automatically reflects across services.

### Database Credentials Note
> [!WARNING]
> Database volumes persist in Docker. If you update the credentials (`PG_USER`, `PG_PASSWORD`, or `PG_DB`) in `.env`, you must delete the old database volume (`docker compose down -v`) for PostgreSQL to apply the new credentials on initialization, otherwise you will encounter `FATAL: password authentication failed` errors.

---

## Directory Layout

- `/gateway` â€” Nginx gateway configuration file.
- `/hub` â€” Express + React code for the authentication and portal switcher app.
- `/defectdojo` â€” Express + React code for vulnerability management.
- `/wazuh` â€” Static React code for the SIEM mockup.

ArtifactMetadata.Summary: Implementation plan for redesigning the authentication architecture to centralize user management, sessions, and login under the Hub microservice as a Single Sign-On (SSO) system, resolving the current database synchronization and in-memory cache issues in the DefectDojo viewer.

Args.CodeContent:
# Centralized Authentication & SSO Redesign Plan

Currently, the Hub and DefectDojo viewer services share the same PostgreSQL database and users table (`defectdojo_viewer_users`). However, because DefectDojo caches the user list in-memory at startup and only re-persists that list on user changes:
1. **Cache Synchronization Inconsistency**: Users created, suspended, or updated on the Hub are not recognized by the DefectDojo backend until its container is restarted.
2. **Data Overwriting**: DefectDojo backend can overwrite database changes with its stale in-memory cached list when calling `saveUsers()`.
3. **Duplication of Auth Concerns**: Both services run duplicate login, session validation, and user management logic.

This plan details how we will redesign the system to achieve **Centralized Authentication (SSO)**, making the Hub the single source of truth for identity, user accounts, and session issuance.

---

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Single Sign-On (SSO) Flow**
> - The login screen in DefectDojo will be entirely removed.
> - If a user navigates to `/defectdojo/` or `/wazuh/` without a valid token, they will be automatically redirected to `/` (the Hub Portal Login).
> - Since all three services are served from the same host/port via Nginx, they share the same origin, allowing them to share local storage (`middleware_token` and `middleware_user`).

> [!WARNING]
> **Centralized User Management UI**
> - The local User Management tab inside the DefectDojo settings page will be removed.
> - All user administration (creating, editing roles, modifying product access list, suspending/activating accounts) will be handled centrally under the **User Management** page of the Hub portal.
> - We will migrate the React UI logic for user administration from DefectDojo to the Hub frontend's `UsersPage`.

---

## Open Questions

> [!NOTE]
> **Are there any API keys or CLI scripts calling DefectDojo's `/api/login` directly?**
> If you have automated scripts logging in via `/api/login` on the DefectDojo port directly, they will need to be updated to post credentials to the Hub's `/api/login` endpoint instead to obtain a JWT.

---

## Proposed Changes

We will group our changes across three components: **Hub Component**, **DefectDojo Component**, and **Gateway Component**.

---

### 1. Hub Component (SSO Identity Provider)

We will implement full User Management in the Hub and make it the exclusive writer/manager of user records.

#### [MODIFY] [server.cjs](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/hub/backend/server.cjs)
- Keep all user CRUD (`/api/users` endpoints) active.
- Ensure passwords are saved securely (already matches DefectDojo's pbkdf2 algorithm).
- Ensure the issued JWT token contains all user details (`username`, `email`, `role`, `products`, `status`).

#### [MODIFY] [UsersPage.jsx](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/hub/src/features/users/UsersPage.jsx)
- Replace the current placeholder content with the full interactive User Management UI.
- We will port the table, modal dialogs, and validation logic from DefectDojo's `UserManagement.jsx`.
- Support:
  - Listing all users.
  - Adding a new user (specifying username, email, password, role, and allowed products list).
  - Editing an existing user (role, email, allowed products, status, and optional password reset).
  - Suspending/activating user accounts.
  - Deleting users (with safeguards to prevent deleting the last admin or yourself).

#### [MODIFY] [UsersPage.css](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/hub/src/features/users/UsersPage.css)
- Style the new user table, form dialogs, input fields, badges, and action buttons to perfectly match the Hub's dark theme aesthetics.

---

### 2. DefectDojo Component (Resource Server)

We will remove the cached user array, duplicate endpoints, and local admin UIs, converting DefectDojo into a stateless client.

#### [MODIFY] [server.cjs](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/defectdojo/backend/server.cjs)
- Remove the global `let users = [];` cache array.
- Remove startup user loaders/migrators (`loadUsers()` and `importUsers()`).
- Modify the `getUsers` and `saveUsers` bridge functions (if referenced elsewhere) to fetch directly from PostgreSQL on demand, or remove them if no longer needed.
- Remove local user-related initialization routines.

#### [MODIFY] [auth.cjs](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/defectdojo/backend/routes/auth.cjs)
- Remove local `/login`, `/users` (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) routes entirely since user CRUD is now handled by the Hub.
- Keep only `/logout` (which clears the local session map if stateful sessions are used, though client-side localStorage purging handles this best).

#### [MODIFY] [auth.cjs](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/defectdojo/backend/security/auth.cjs)
- Update the `createRequireAuth` middleware:
  - It will decode the JWT signed by the Hub's secret.
  - **Dynamic Status Check**: To prevent suspended or deleted users from using unexpired tokens, the middleware will run a quick read-only check against the database:
    ```javascript
    const { rows } = await db.query('SELECT status FROM defectdojo_viewer_users WHERE username = $1', [payload.username]);
    if (!rows.length || rows[0].status === 'suspended') {
        return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Unauthorized: Account is inactive or deleted' });
    }
    ```
  - This ensures real-time account suspension works without keeping any in-memory list.

#### [MODIFY] [Settings.jsx](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/defectdojo/src/features/settings/Settings.jsx)
- Remove the `User Management` tab from the Settings tabs list.
- If the user is an admin, show a link/button that navigates back to the Hub portal's user management page (`/` or `/#users`).

#### [DELETE] [UserManagement](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/defectdojo/src/features/settings/UserManagement)
- Delete the folder containing `UserManagement.jsx` and `UserManagement.css` to clean up the codebase.

---

### 3. Gateway Component

We will secure the gateway configuration.

#### [MODIFY] [nginx.conf](file:///c:/Users/ifilm/à¹€à¸”à¸ªà¸à¹Œà¸—à¹‡à¸­à¸›/Scan%20CSV%20File/defectdojo-viewer/gateway/nginx.conf)
- Ensure `/api/login` and `/api/users` requests on the root path route strictly to the Hub.
- Remove or block any old user-management routes on the `/defectdojo/api` path for extra security.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
- Validate that the Nginx configuration is valid:
  `docker compose exec gateway nginx -t`
- Build and restart all microservices:
  `docker compose down`
  `docker compose up -d --build`

### Manual Verification
1. **Centralized Login Flow**:
   - Access `http://localhost/defectdojo/` in an incognito window. Verify you are automatically redirected to `http://localhost/` (Hub login).
   - Log in with valid credentials. Verify you are logged into the Hub portal.
   - Click the "DefectDojo Viewer" workspace card. Verify you can access the findings dashboard without logging in again.
2. **Centralized User CRUD**:
   - Navigate to `http://localhost/#users` (or click User Management on the Hub).
   - Create a new user with `viewer` role and access to specific products.
   - Edit the user's details, then suspend the user.
   - Verify that the suspended user is immediately locked out of both the Hub and the DefectDojo Viewer (API calls return 401).
   - Reactivate the user and verify access is restored.
   - Try to delete the user and verify the deletion is reflected instantly.
3. **Database Consistency**:
   - Inspect the PostgreSQL database directly after editing/creating users to verify the records are correct.
   - Restart the `defectdojo` container and confirm that user details/credentials and access privileges persist perfectly without database overwrites.
